proposed_value:
- E1 enhancer sequences are significantly enriched for FOS and JUN motifs, while E2 sequences are not significantly enriched for any particular motif (Benjamini-Hochberg corrected P < 0.05; Extended Data Fig. 6b,c and Supplementary Table 5).
- E1 sequences show stronger biochemical features of active enhancers, including higher H3K27ac, DNase I hypersensitivity, and AP-1 factor binding (JUN and ATF3) compared to E2 sequences (Fig. 3a, Extended Data Fig. 6a-d).
- Despite similar average activity in ExP-STARR-seq assays, E1 sequences have stronger effects on gene expression in CRISPR perturbation experiments and are more likely to be predicted as enhancers across cell types (94% of E1 vs. 49% of E2 in K562 cells; 32% of E1 vs. 13% of E2 in >50 of 130 other biosamples).
- Both E1 and E2 genomic enhancers produce enhancer RNAs (GRO-cap) and show similar sequence conservation (Extended Data Fig. 6g,h).
- The ExP-STARR-seq assay may detect activity for sequences not active in their endogenous chromosomal context, possibly due to episomal effects or non-transcriptional mechanisms (Extended Data Fig. 4b; references 16, 17, 29).
- The study includes 65 genes with previously studied enhancers in CRISPR experiments in K562 cells (reference 22), 715 genes spanning a range of promoter activities (including top 200 expressed genes and 515 random expressed genes), and 20 genes not expressed in K562 but active in GM12878 and HCT-116 cells (top 70% by TPM; reference 1).
